To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
‘The mental text entry application “Hex-o-Spell” is the world’s first application that allows a user to type with their thoughts at a speed comparable to that of normal text entry’.
1) the mental spelling interface Hex-o-Spell provides robust, fast and intuitive text entry, and 2) it is possible to use BCI systems for real world applications.
a) BCI feedback design should be based on HCI research, and b) the visual display should be utilized as a communication channel for feedback, and not just for display.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of Human-Computer interaction principles to the design and implementation of BCI applications.
the design of intelligent front-ends for BCI systems, and with the application of BCI technology to real-world tasks.
the development of a mental text entry interface for BCI applications which combines principles of Human- Computer Interaction research with the requirements of a BCI system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is effective, robust, and easy to use.
Hex-o-Spell represents a major step forward in the field of BCI applications, and that it can be used as a model for the design of other BCI applications.
the Hex-o-Spell system provides a very good compromise between robustness of control and speed of operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hex-o-Spell system is a robust, efficient and user-friendly mental text entry system.
the Hex-o-Spell interface is a good example of a well-designed BCI front-end.
the design of the mental text entry interface ‘Hex-o-Spill’ is robust and efficient, and that it has the potential to become a useful tool for people with motor disabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of BCI feedback is a crucial aspect for the success of the system.
a high visual display bandwidth can help compensate for the limited control bandwidth of BCIs.
the principles of HCI are also applicable to BCIs, and that a BCI can be designed to be as effective as any other input device.
